books.section: American Involvement in Vietnam, World War II–1963

primary_sources: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, Public Law 88-408, August 7, 1964 (paraphrased)

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, Public Law 88-408

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, Public Law 88-408, passed August 7, 1964 (public domain, U.S. government document). Vote totals from the Congressional Record.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, passed August 7, 1964. After reports that North Vietnamese boats had fired on American destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin, Congress approved a resolution giving President Lyndon Johnson power to take all necessary steps, including the use of armed force, to prevent further aggression in Southeast Asia. The House voted 416 to 0. The Senate voted 88 to 2.

stem: The near-unanimous votes for the resolution best show which of the following about Congress in August 1964?

options.text: Congress refused to give the president any new war powers
options.misconception: Congress gave the president broad power to use armed force, so it did not refuse him.

options.text: Congress broadly accepted the president's account and his request for power
Congress declared a formal state of war against North Vietnam
options.misconception: Background: Congress never declared war on North Vietnam; the resolution authorized force without a declaration.

options.text: Congress voted to end all American involvement in Vietnam
options.misconception: The resolution expanded the president's power to fight in Vietnam; it did not end involvement.

rationales.A: The resolution gave Johnson power to use armed force, so Congress granted new war powers rather than refusing them.
rationales.B: Background: the House voted 416 to 0 and the Senate 88 to 2, so Congress accepted the president's account and his request.
rationales.C: Background: the United States never declared war on North Vietnam; the resolution authorized force without a declaration.
rationales.D: The resolution expanded the president's power to act in Vietnam, the opposite of ending involvement.
rationales.general:
1. The passage reports the votes: 416 to 0 in the House and 88 to 2 in the Senate.
2. A vote that lopsided means almost every member accepted the case as presented.
3. Background: the case was the president's report of attacks on American destroyers and his request for power to act.
4. Congress therefore handed the president broad war powers on the strength of his account.
Remember: A near-unanimous vote usually means the chamber accepted the story it was given.
